overview: Mint B1's Disabler is a kitchen-sink packet interceptor: a single onEvent dispatcher branches on receive, send, motion and update events and applies whatever subset of its 45 settings are enabled. Modes are named for the anticheats and servers they target (Watchdog2020, Verus, Karhu, NCP, Spartan, Redesky, Warzone, Zonecraft, Hazel, PurplePrison, Matrix, Kauri, MineLatino, Supercraft) plus a row of generic primitives: C0F transaction corruption, C00 keepalive key rewriting, C0B entity-action spam, C07 digging spam, C08 placement spam, C13 abilities injection, C16 respawn spam, C18 spectate spoofs and C0C input spoofs. The dominant technique is queue-and-flush: packets are cancelled, parked in one of three queues, and released in bursts through sendPacketNoEvent on a timer, so the server receives everything late and out of phase. The file also carries a heavy load of dead code, empty stub modes and at least one guaranteed ClassCastException.

sections.p: All logic lives in one method: onEvent(Event) branches on instanceof across EventReceivePacket, EventSendPacket, EventMotion and EventUpdate. State is kept in three ConcurrentLinkedDeque packet queues (a general queue, a C0F-only queue, and a never-used C00-only queue), a shared Timer with two independent clocks, and a handful of flags. Cross-module communication is done through public statics: hypixelStrafe and desyncrot are written here and read elsewhere in Mint, and vulcanyaw is used as a scratch register between the NCP and Kauri modes.

The queue-and-flush pattern appears in nearly every mode: cancel the packet, park it, and release the backlog through sendPacketNoEvent on a timer (15s for Watchdog2020, 400ms for Verus, 1-2s random for Redesky/Spartan, 5412ms and 1337ms for Warzone's two queues, 690ms/2500ms for Zonecraft, 1550ms for VerusCombat, 505ms/200ms for MineLatino/Supercraft). Field corruption rewrites C0F uids to 1337 and ids to 69, C00 keys to 1337, and C13 packets to claim flying, creative, and invulnerable. Movement bypasses add constant y drift (Karhu 0.015625, Redesky 0.000125), send mirrored C04 position pairs 9 blocks ahead and behind (NCP), rewrite C04/C06 to void coordinates (PurplePrison), or alternate onGround flags (Zonecraft). The receive side cancels S08 teleports and re-sends them as C06 (Redesky, NCP) and cancels S12 velocity.

The file is accretion-heavy: settings like HypixelTimerTest, Spartan, mineLatino and watchdog are declared with UI labels but their handlers are empty or absent; packetQueueC00Only, the x/y/z/yaw/pitch fields, transactiontype, placetype and NumberSetting are dead; and getXZDifference is called with packet.x twice (a copy-paste bug). The Hazel mode casts a C0F transaction to C00PacketKeepAlive, which throws ClassCastException the first time the branch runs, and the NCP module scan compares module names with == instead of equals(). The ModeDisplay setting is a 31-option mirror of every toggle, used only for the HUD label.

annotations.text: Package declaration: the module lives in Mint's exploit package, grouped with the anticheat-facing utilities.

Java collections imports: ArrayList and List are never used in this file, but Queue, UUID (for the spectate spoof), ConcurrentLinkedDeque (the three packet queues), Comparator and Collectors (the interact-target sort/filter) are all live.
Apache Commons RandomUtils and LWJGL Keyboard imports. RandomUtils is not used anywhere in this file; Keyboard.KEY_F supplies the module's default keybind in the constructor.

Mint framework imports: the Epsilon client singleton, the Event base class, the four event types this module handles (EventMotion, EventUpdate, EventReceivePacket, EventSendPacket), the Module base class and ModuleManager, the Fly module from movement (referenced by name in the NCP module scan), the BooleanSetting/ModeSetting/NumberSetting settings framework (NumberSetting is imported but never used), and the MoveUtil and Timer helpers.

Vanilla 1.8.9 packet imports: the serverbound play classes C00 keepalive, C01 chat, C02 use entity, C03 player (plus the C04 position, C05 look and C06 poslook subclasses), C07 digging, C0B entity action, C0C input, C0D close window, C0F transaction, C10 creative action, C11 enchant, C12 sign, C13 abilities, C15 settings, C16 status, C18 spectate, and the received S08 poslook and S12 velocity. Several imports (C0D, C11, C12, C15) are never referenced; the file grew by accretion.

More vanilla imports in no particular order: BlockPos and EnumFacing (used by the dig/place helpers), then C17 custom payload, C08 block placement, C09 held item change and C0A animation. C17, C09 and C0A are dead imports; C08 is used by the place() helper.

World, entity and client imports: BlockAir (the NCP ground check), Minecraft, EntityPlayerSP, GuiChest/GuiInventory (GuiChest only appears in comments), NetHandlerPlayClient, Entity and EntityLivingBase (interact targeting), EntityBoat (dead), PlayerCapabilities (dead), Blocks and ItemBlock/ItemStack (the stone placement spoof) and the Packet base type used by the queues.
Class declaration: Disabler extends Module, Mint's module base. Every module follows this shape; the constructor registers name, keybind, category and description.
The main packet queue. Packets are parked here when a mode cancels them, then flushed in a burst later via sendPacketNoEvent so the server still receives everything, just late.
A second queue used only by the Warzone mode to hold C0F transactions separately from the general queue, so they flush on a different timer.
A third queue for keepalives only. Declared but never written or read anywhere in the file: leftover from an earlier iteration of the Warzone mode.
Coordinate fields x, y, z, yaw, pitch. Never assigned anywhere in the file; dead fields.

Static flags shared with other modules: hypixelStrafe is set false on enable/disable and read by Mint's movement code, desyncrot is set by the RotationDesync mode and consumed elsewhere in the client. Public statics are Mint's cross-module communication mechanism.

Private mode state: matrixswitch is set false on enable and never read; verusVoid gates the empty Verus receive stub; watchdogStrafed is set by the HypixelStrafe mode when the server teleports the player.
The module's Timer, shared by every queue-and-flush mode. hasTimeElapsed and hasTimeElapsed2 give the two independent flush clocks the Warzone mode needs.
Watchdog2020 toggle: the 2020 Hypixel Watchdog bypass. Delays every C0F transaction 15 seconds and force-flags every outgoing C13 abilities packet as flying (see the send handler).
SpigotData toggle: nudges every received S08 teleport up by 1.0E-4 blocks, a spoof aimed at Spigot's teleport confirmation checks.
C0FData toggle: rewrites every outgoing C0F transaction to uid 1337 with accepted=false, corrupting the server's transaction bookkeeping.
C00Key toggle: rewrites every outgoing C00 keepalive key to 1337.

HypixelStrafe toggle: the strafe bypass. Once the server teleports the player (S08), every non-C06 serverbound packet is cancelled so the server only ever sees the C06 confirmations (see receive/send handlers).
HypixelTimerTest toggle: an empty stub block in the send handler; the setting does nothing.
KarhuMovement toggle: adds 0.015625 to the y of every EventMotion, a tiny constant drift aimed at Karhu's movement checks.
Verus toggle: queues every serverbound packet for 400ms and rewrites C0F transaction ids to 69. The receive handler has a paired verusVoid stub.

NCP toggle: the main NoCheapPlus bypass. Accepts S08 teleports by immediately echoing a C06 poslook, and while moving, sends a mirrored pair of C04 positions 9 blocks ahead and behind (see both handlers).
NCPModulCheck toggle: gates the NCP movement bypass on whether a movement module is enabled and whether Fly specifically is running, to avoid fighting other modules.
PurplePrison toggle: after tick 60, adds 0.015625 to every C03 y; after tick 100, every 100 ticks rewrites C04/C06 positions to (0, -50000, 0); between ticks 61 and 99 it cancels C0F transactions.
Spartan toggle: an empty stub in the receive handler; in the send handler it joins the rede mode's queue-and-random-flush block.
Redesky toggle: cancels S08 teleports and re-sends them itself, cancels S12 velocity, and in the send handler queues every packet with a random 1-2 second flush.
Warzone toggle: queues C00 keepalives and C0F transactions in separate queues and flushes them on two different randomized timers (see send handler).
MineLatino toggle: delays every serverbound packet by 505ms (see the shared ml/superc block).
Zonecraft toggle: delays every packet 690ms (2500ms for C00/C0F), slows the game timer to 0.8, and flips C03 onGround to tick parity while airborne.

Hazel toggle: the largest single mode. Randomizes C0F/C00 keys and C06 y / C05 pitch-yaw on a tick schedule, cancels sprint actions, parks packets in the queue, injects flying C13 abilities, and flushes every 120 ticks (see send handler).
MatrixSemiStrafe toggle: adds a sub-millimeter sinusoidal jitter to EventMotion x/z on alternating ticks, aimed at Matrix's strafe checks.
SupercraftSkywars toggle: the same packet delay as MineLatino but with a 200ms delay and it also feeds the mode display list.

VerusLatestFly toggle: the flight bypass. While grounded it records groundpos, and while airborne it spams stone block placements at (posX, posY - groundpos, posZ) (see the EventUpdate handler and the place() helper).
A setting labeled 'Test' that is never referenced by any handler. Dead setting, probably a leftover experiment slot.
Matrix4.04Damage toggle: every 4 ticks sends a C0B RIDING_JUMP entity action (the Matrix damage exploit), and on enable it prints usage instructions to chat.
VerusCombat toggle: delays C0F transactions by 1550ms (1565ms when a C02 use-entity was just sent), pairing combat packets with delayed confirmations for Verus.

KauriMovement toggle: on enable it snapshots cameraYaw into vulcanyaw; every motion tick it sets the event yaw to that value, and on even ticks to -3141 while nudging movement with packetComedy (see EventMotion handler).

RotationDesync toggle: sets the static desyncrot flag once the terrain is loaded, signalling Mint's rotation code to desynchronize server/client rotations. The placement code that used to accompany it is commented out.
Interact toggle: every even tick sends a C02 INTERACT to the nearest living entity within range, keeping the server busy with interaction packets (see EventMotion handler).
EntityAction toggle: master switch for the C0B entity-action spammer below, which sends the action selected by the et mode setting every tick.
EntityActType mode setting: selects which C0B action the spammer sends, defaulting to Jump, with Sneak, StopSneak, Sprint, Stop Sprint, Sleep and Inventory options.
EntityTargetMode mode setting: Self or Random. Only ever compared against 'Self' in a dead-code block (see line 699); Random has no implementation.
VoidTP toggle: every 20 ticks forces the EventMotion y to -1, dropping the player toward the void for a teleport-based check bypass.
GoofyC0C toggle: every 4 ticks sends a C0C input packet with both axes at Float.MAX_VALUE, an absurd-input spoof for input checks.
Input toggle: sends a fresh zeroed C0C input packet every tick.
Dig toggle: master switch for the C07 digging spammer, which sends START_DESTROY_BLOCK at the position chosen by digtype.
DigType mode setting: where the fake dig targets, defaulting to Under (one block below the player), with Self, OutOfBounds (12 blocks offset) and Unloaded (coordinates multiplied by 256).
Place toggle: spams C08 stone placements one block below the player every tick.
Placetype mode setting: declared with Under/Self/OutOfBounds/Unloaded options but never read anywhere; the place spam always uses the Under position.
ConfirmTransaction toggle: delays C0F transactions by 1550ms (1565ms after a C02), sharing the VerusCombat code path.
TransType mode setting: Delayed or Cancel. Never read by the handlers; the confirmation path always delays rather than cancels.
CreativeAction toggle: every tick sends a C10 creative inventory action with a null item stack at slot 1, a creative-mode spoof.
Abilities toggle: sends a fresh C13 abilities packet every tick.
Respawn toggle: sends a C16 PERFORM_RESPAWN client status every tick.
Spectate toggle: every tick sends a C18 spectate packet with a random UUID, desynchronizing the server's spectated entity.
ModeDisplay setting: a 31-option mode list whose sole purpose is the module's on-screen display (displayInfo), mirroring every toggle in the module. Purely cosmetic.
vulcanyaw: a float reused as a scratch value. The NCP motion code stores a y-offset in it and the Kauri mode reads it back as a yaw. Shared-state hack between two otherwise unrelated modes.
groundpos: the y position recorded by VerusLatestFly while the player is grounded, used as the offset for the airborne block placements.

Constructor: registers the module as 'Disabler' with keybind F, the EXPLOIT category and the description 'Cripples anticheats', then registers all 45 settings in one addSettings call. The mode display setting is registered last.

onEnable: resets the Verus and strafe state flags, restarts the flush timer and clears the main queue so no stale packets survive from a previous session. If VerusLatestFly is on it warns that the bypass needs an empty hand; if Matrix4.04Damage is on it prints the damage exploit instructions. The Kauri mode snapshots cameraYaw into vulcanyaw and hypixelStrafe is forced false.

onDisable: clears the rotation-desync and strafe flags, un-marks the player as dead (a leftover isDead guard from a damage exploit), then flushes every parked packet via sendPacketNoEvent and empties the queue. Disabling mid-bypass dumps the backlog instead of dropping it, so the server still sees the delayed packets.

The single event dispatcher. Every Mint event type funnels through onEvent; the handler branches on instanceof for EventReceivePacket, EventSendPacket, EventMotion and EventUpdate. This is the whole module's logic in one method.
Receive branch: only runs once the net handler exists, and pulls the raw packet object out of the event. Everything below reacts to packets coming back from the server.
HypixelStrafe trigger: once the terrain is loaded, an S08 teleport sets watchdogStrafed. The send handler then uses this flag to cancel everything except C06 confirmations.
SpigotData: every received S08 has its y nudged up by 1.0E-4. The tiny mismatch between the echoed position and the client's real position is the Spigot teleport-check spoof.
Verus receive stub: guarded by verusVoid (which nothing ever sets to true) and empty. The Verus bypass is entirely send-side; this block is a placeholder.

NCP teleport accept: when an S08 arrives after terrain load, the module immediately echoes a C06 poslook to the teleport destination with onGround=true so the server sees the position accepted. The acceptedX/acceptedZ booleans are computed with getXZDifference but never used (and the call passes packet.x twice, a copy-paste bug), and the m/fly locals are dead. The net effect is just the immediate C06 echo.
Spartan receive stub: guarded by doneLoadingTerrain and completely empty. The Spartan handling is send-side only.

Redesky: cancels every S08 teleport and re-sends the position itself as a C06 with the client's real onGround state, keeping the server's view while suppressing the client-side snap. Also cancels every S12 velocity packet, freezing knockback.
Send branch: runs once the player and net handler exist, and only after the terrain has finished loading. p is the outgoing packet; most modes below cancel it, mutate it, or both.

HypixelStrafe lockdown: once the S08 trigger fired, every serverbound packet except C06 poslook confirmations is cancelled. The server only ever sees the C06 stream, which is the strafe desync the bypass wants.

Watchdog2020 transaction delay: C0F transactions are cancelled and parked in the queue; every 15 seconds the whole queue is flushed via sendPacketNoEvent. The server gets all transactions, just 15 seconds late, which breaks Watchdog's timing correlation.
Watchdog2020 abilities inject: every C03 movement packet is shadowed by an extra C13 abilities packet added to the send queue.
Watchdog2020 flying flag: every outgoing C13 abilities packet has flying forced true, claiming flight capability the player does not have.
C0FData: every C0F transaction is rewritten with uid 1337 and accepted=false. The server's transaction counter and the client's never agree, breaking the anticheat's transaction validation.
C00Key: every outgoing C00 keepalive has its key rewritten to 1337. The server echoes the wrong key back, so keepalive-based reachability checks misfire.

Verus: every serverbound packet is cancelled and queued; C0F transactions additionally get their id rewritten to 69. Every 400ms the queue flushes. Constant short delay plus corrupted transaction ids is the Verus bypass.

Hazel C0F branch: intended to randomize the transaction and park it, but it casts the C0F packet to C00PacketKeepAlive (line 330), which throws ClassCastException the moment a C0F actually arrives at tick % 3 == 1. This branch can never complete; the code is broken.
Hazel C00 branch: every third tick (ticksExisted % 3 == 1) a C00 keepalive gets a random key (Math.random + PI + E), is queued and cancelled. The server sees randomized keepalive keys.
Hazel C0B branch: every third tick the entity action is cancelled, queued, and re-sent 4000ms later via sendPacketNoEventDelayed.

Hazel C06 branch: every 40 ticks a C06 poslook has onGround forced false and y randomized, then it is cancelled and queued. The fake y poisons the server's position tracker before the real position lands.
Hazel C05 branch: every 40 ticks a look packet is marked rotating with pitch and yaw randomized, then cancelled and queued. Randomized rotations desync rotation checks.
Hazel sprint cancel: every START_SPRINTING entity action is cancelled outright, so the server never sees the player sprint.
Hazel flush: every 120 ticks the entire parked queue is flushed via sendPacketNoEvent and cleared. This is the Hazel mode's release clock.
Hazel abilities inject: every C03 movement packet is shadowed by a fresh C13 abilities packet.
Hazel abilities flags: every outgoing C13 has allowFlying, creativeMode, invulnerable and flying all forced true. The server is told the player is a flying invulnerable creative player.
HypixelTimerTest stub: an empty block. The setting exists in the UI and does nothing in code.
PurplePrison post-tick-60 phase: every C03 movement packet has 0.015625 added to its y, a constant upward drift the server's movement validator tolerates.

PurplePrison early phase: between ticks 61 and 99, every C0F transaction is cancelled outright. After tick 100, every 100 ticks C04/C06 positions are rewritten to (0, -50000, 0), a void position designed to break the anticheat's ground-distance sampling.

Redesky/Spartan shared path: every serverbound packet is cancelled and queued, and the queue flushes after a random 1-2 seconds (1000 * (Math.random + 1) ms). Random-period packet delay defeats timed checks on both anticheats.

Zonecraft: skips the first tick, slows the game timer to 0.8x, then cancels every packet and re-sends it delayed (690ms normally, 2500ms for C00/C0F). While airborne, C03 onGround is rewritten to tick parity, alternating ground flags the server cannot reconcile with the timer slowdown.

Warzone: C00 keepalives go into the main queue and C0F transactions into the C0f-only queue, both cancelled. The main queue flushes after 5412 + up to 6ms of jitter, the C0F queue after 1337 + up to 6ms. Two independent flush clocks keep the two packet types out of phase.

VerusCombat / ConfirmTransaction: C0F transactions are cancelled and re-sent 1550ms later (1565ms if a C02 use-entity preceded them). The extra 15ms after combat packets is the Verus combat-check timing offset.

MineLatino/Supercraft: once the network manager exists and the player is past tick 0, every packet is cancelled and re-sent delayed (505ms for MineLatino, 200ms for Supercraft). Chat messages pass through untouched. The commented-out lines show an earlier attempt to also rewrite onGround and y inside the delayed C03 stream.
EventMotion branch: fires on every client motion tick. The event carries the position and rotation that will be sent; several modes rewrite it in place before the packet is built.
KarhuMovement: adds 0.015625 to the motion event's y every tick. The constant tiny drift is the Karhu bypass.
NCP motion: while the player is moving, the event is forced onGround=true, so every movement packet claims to be grounded.

NCP motion math: converts the player's yaw to radians and computes expected positions 9 blocks ahead of the player along the facing direction (sin/cos of the yaw scaled by 9). The 9-block offset is the NCP teleport-distance threshold the bypass works against.

NCP motion height: if jump is held the phantom position goes 5 blocks up, if sneak is held 5 down, otherwise level. The chosen offset is then stored into vulcanyaw as a float, the scratch-value hack the Kauri mode later reads as a yaw.
m and fly locals declared true/false, mirroring the dead locals in the receive handler. They are reassigned by the NCP module scan below.

NCPModulCheck scan: walks every enabled module and sets m=true when any MOVEMENT-category module is active, and fly=true when a module named 'Fly' is found. The name comparison uses == on strings instead of equals(), which only works because module names are interned literals.

NCP phantom position pair: when the module check passes (or is disabled), the module sends a C04 position 9 blocks ahead with the chosen height offset, then a second C04 9 blocks behind at ground level. The mirrored pair is what desynchronizes NCP's movement prediction. The branch splits on whether the player is airborne or standing on air, with slightly different height handling per case. Both sends go through addToSendQueue so they are not re-intercepted by this handler.
Redesky motion: for the first 69 ticks after terrain load, 0.000125 is added to the motion event's y. A tiny startup drift paired with the receive-side teleport rejection.

Interact targeting: on pre-motion ticks, gathers all living entities, filters out the player, dead entities and anything within 1 block, sorts by distance, and on even ticks sends a C02 INTERACT to the nearest one. The targets.equals(null) guard is meaningless (a list is never null here, and equals(null) is always false).
MatrixSemiStrafe: on even ticks the motion event is shifted by sin(yaw * 0.001) on x and z, on odd ticks by the negated value. The alternating sub-millimeter jitter is the Matrix strafe desync.
CreativeAction: sends a C10 creative inventory action with a null item stack into slot 1 every tick, spoofing creative inventory writes.

KauriMovement: every motion tick the event yaw is set to the vulcanyaw scratch value (which the NCP mode populated with a height offset, so the yaw is garbage but consistent). On even ticks it is overwritten with -3141 and, if any movement key is held, packetComedy nudges the motion by -0.1. Odd ticks create an unused MoveUtil. The randomized absurd yaw is the Kauri rotation bypass.
VoidTP: every 20 ticks the motion event's y is forced to -1, dropping the reported position toward the void on a fixed schedule.
First EventUpdate branch: the module's on-screen display text is set to the current ModeDisplay mode name, so the HUD shows which bypass is active.
Second EventUpdate branch: creates a fresh MoveUtil, then handles the pre/post phases of the update event.

VerusLatestFly: while grounded, groundpos records the player's y. While airborne, the place() helper spams C08 stone placements at (posX, posY - groundpos, posZ), one block per tick below where the player was when grounded. The block spam keeps the player grounded from the server's perspective while flying. The block-relative and swing-item variants are commented out.

RotationDesync: once terrain is loaded, the static desyncrot flag is set, which Mint's rotation code picks up to desynchronize rotations. The C08 placement spam that used to accompany this mode is commented out.
Dead code: checks the EntityTargetMode setting with == against 'Self' and assigns the player to a local that is never used. The Random mode has no implementation here.
Third EventUpdate branch: the Matrix4.04Damage mode sends a C0B RIDING_JUMP entity action every 4 ticks, and the Input mode sends a zeroed C0C input packet every tick.
Pre-update spam, part one: GoofyC0C sends a C0C input packet with both axes at Float.MAX_VALUE every 4 ticks.
Pre-update spam, part two: Spectate sends a C18 spectate packet with a random UUID every tick.
Pre-update spam, part three: Place sends a C08 stone placement one block below the player every tick, with facing (0.5, 0.5, 0.5) and the stone item stack sourced from the world.

Dig spammer: sends a C07 START_DESTROY_BLOCK every tick at the position chosen by digtype. Under targets one block below the player, Self targets the player's own block, OutOfBounds offsets by 12 on all axes, and Unloaded multiplies the coordinates by 256 to hit far-out-of-range positions.

EntityAction spammer: sends one C0B entity action per tick, with the action selected by the et mode setting: Jump maps to RIDING_JUMP, Sneak to START_SNEAKING, StopSneak to STOP_SNEAKING, Sprint to START_SPRINTING, StopSprint to STOP_SPRINTING, Sleep to STOP_SLEEPING and Inventory to OPEN_INVENTORY.
Respawn: sends a C16 PERFORM_RESPAWN client status every tick.
Abilities: sends a fresh C13 abilities packet every tick.

place() helper: wraps C08 block placement construction for the VerusLatestFly spam. Direct addToSendQueue means the packet bypasses the send event, so the module never re-processes its own placements.
